speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this dry cough going on for about three months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but it does make me feel quite winded when I try to play basketball. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of three months suggests a chronic issue rather than an acute infection. Have you noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or a history of smoking? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrates or obvious masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of hyperinflated lungs and flattened diaphragms are classic signs of air trapping. Do you have a history of smoking, and do you experience wheezing or shortness of breath during activities other than basketball?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been smoking a pack a day for twenty years, and I definitely get short of breath when I climb stairs or carry groceries, not just when playing basketball. I haven't noticed any whistling sounds in my chest, but the cough just won't go away. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
